ShopBot Index › Beyond UCP › Product data

How many stores have structured product data?

In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 161 of 271 stores we could check have schema.org Product markup on a product page we fetched (59.4%). Of those, 141 include price, currency and availability and 20 have Product markup without all three. Left out of the share: 2,583 stores we couldn't check (we could not reach a product page). A refusal is not "no". A published file or profile is a declaration, not proof that agents can buy. ShopBot Index does not test purchases.

Big retailers first (29): American Eagle Outfitters, Asprey, Carrefour, Church's, Clas Ohlson, Detskiy Mir, Dollar General, FAO Schwarz, Flying Tiger Copenhagen, Foot Locker, Fruit of the Loom, Globus, Imperial Porcelain Factory, Intimissimi, J.Crew, Lidl, Magnit, Manor, Marks & Spencer, MediaMarkt, Mexx, On AG, Oniverse, Poundland, Rite Aid, River Island, The Body Shop, Ulta Beauty and Zappos.

How we check

We fetch one page that looks like a product page, from a link on the home page or, if there is none, from at most two sitemap files. Full means schema.org Product or ProductGroup markup, or microdata itemtype of schema.org/Product, with an Offer or AggregateOffer that has a price, a currency and availability. Partial means Product markup without all three. None means the page we fetched had no Product markup. A store is one we could check when at least one website landed in full, partial or none. If we could not reach a product page, the store is left out. See schema.org Product. A store counts when at least one of its websites meets the rule. This page counts stores. The Beyond UCP table counts websites, so the two numbers can differ. How we check.
